classification.recommended_terminology: Smarandache function (also called the Kempner function), S(q)=min{k>=1:q divides k!}

primary_sources.title: Miscellanea
primary_sources.author: A. J. Kempner
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Section II, 'Concerning the smallest integer m! divisible by a given integer n': the factorial-divisibility function later written S(n)=min{k:n divides k!}.
primary_sources.supports: The historical arithmetic object, not the factorial-gap carry implication.

primary_sources.title: Polynomial analogue of the Smarandache function
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Introduction, p. 1: defines the integer function as the least k with n|k!, says Kempner gave the first correct algorithm, notes Smarandache's rediscovery, and records that it is also called the Kempner function.
primary_sources.supports: Current conventional terminology and historical attribution.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The factorial-gap series, the carry theorem, a finite m=300000 certificate, or irrationality.

primary_sources.title: On the composition of a certain arithmetic function
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Abstract: S(n) is the smallest positive k with n|k!.
primary_sources.supports: Use of S(n) as a standard arithmetic-function notation.

primary_sources.title: Solution 6674: The smallest factorial that is a multiple of n
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Published solution record for the same smallest-factorial problem; a modern mathematical treatment of the standard function, not a source for the factorial-gap carry consumer.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The source-specific carry implication or any irrationality conclusion.

mechanism_comparison.standard_core: S(q)>=m is exactly equivalent to q not dividing (m-1)!.
mechanism_comparison.source_specific_delta: The Lean theorem derives that standard condition from one non-unit carry of the factorial-gap series under a displayed rational representation.
mechanism_comparison.finite_consumer: The module's m=60 certificate gives q not dividing 59!. A separately certified m=300000 carry gives the finite q not dividing 299999! screen.
mechanism_comparison.why_not_endpoint_progress: One finite factorial-divisibility exclusion constrains possible rational denominators but does not rule out all denominators, prove cofinally many carries, or prove irrationality.

evidence_class_split.m=300000: exact finite GMP certificate consumed by Lean theorem; not a cofinal result

observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.evidence_class: Standard externally sourced arithmetic-function definition plus a source-specific Lean-checked finite denominator consumer; the m=60 and m=300000 certificates are exact finite evidence only.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.closest_known_result: Kempner, American Mathematical Monthly 25 (1918), Section II, introduced the smallest-factorial-multiple problem; Li--Sha (2020), Introduction, and Luca--Sándor (2009), Abstract, use the modern Smarandache/Kempner-function terminology S(q)=min{k:q|k!}.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.comparison_relation: The equivalence S(q)≥m iff q∤(m−1)! is the definition-level smoothness screen, not new number theory. The source-specific delta is the Lean implication from one displayed non-unit factorial carry to that screen under the rational-representation hypothesis. It is subordinate to the existing factorial carry-characterization endpoint and separate from the continued-fraction size screen.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.exact_delta: A non-unit carry at index m transfers to S(q)≥m, equivalently q∤(m−1)!, so even arbitrarily large (m−1)-smooth denominators are excluded by that finite certificate. No assertion is made about all rational denominators or a cofinal carry supply.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.disconfirming_evidence: The finite m=60/m=300000 screens do not imply a global denominator contradiction. The current FactorialZeroPlateau source changed only the surrounding terminology to ‘Smarandache function (also called the Kempner function)’; it adds no cofinal or irrationality theorem. Kempner/Li--Sha/Luca--Sándor do not support the factorial-gap carry implication.
